ready2_open_rewrite.final_cot: Image description: The figure shows a blue square-wave signal on an oscilloscope grid, and two adjacent narrow high-level pulses can be seen. Taking two consecutive rising edges as one complete period for observation, the horizontal distance between the two rising edges is about 5 major divisions; the horizontal width of a single pulse at the high level is about 0.5 major divisions. Reasoning: duty cycle = high-level time / period × 100%. Substituting the grid readings gives: 0.5 / 5 × 100% = 10.0%.

raw_record.question_text: Determine the duty cycle of this square wave signal, as shown in the figure. The duty cycle is ______%.

method.method_draft: First inspect the waveform grid and identify one complete cycle by taking two consecutive rising edges. Count the horizontal grid divisions between these rising edges to get the period, about 5 divisions. Then count the horizontal width of the high-level portion of one pulse, about 0.5 division. Compute duty cycle as high-time divided by period times 100, giving 0.5/5 × 100 = 10.0%.
